question.text: Under the SEBI (AIF) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2025 co-investment framework, Angel Funds specifically:

answer.text: Must launch a CIV scheme for every investment exceeding INR 5 crore
Shall not launch any CIV schemes
May only launch CIV schemes for listed equity investments
Are exempt from shelf placement memorandum filing

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.9 (Co-investments in AIFs), while Category I and II AIFs can launch CIV schemes, the 2025 regulation explicitly provides that Angel Funds shall NOT launch any CIV schemes. Angel Funds retain their unique accredited-investor investor-base structure and distinct regulatory treatment. The Trap: Angel Funds are Cat I sub-category but are specifically carved out of CIV eligibility. The 5-crore threshold and listed-equity limit are invented. Cross-Exam Context: Angel Fund restrictions also tested in XIX-A (Cat I distributor) — the no-CIV rule is a specific XIX-C addition. Manager's Pro-Tip: If you run a sponsor platform that has both a VC Fund and an Angel Fund, route co-investment deals through the VC Fund's CIV — not the Angel Fund — to stay on the right side of the 2025 carve-out.
